a_threshold_that_was_the_finding: the first version asked whether anything was taken within forty blocks of a heading, and reported Enphase's '13. COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES' as unreached. The selector had taken a block fifty-seven blocks into that note. The window was the finding, not the filing, so the distance is now recorded and judged rather than compared to a number.
and_it_accepts_nothing: D02 stays out of the acceptance register. The other direction - whether the excerpts that were taken are the right ones - is done for one filing, Pfizer, and it found two wrong blocks there. Knowing no note was missed does not make the set that was taken correct.
method: heading-shaped means short, emphasised and not a link - the same shape the route's own note-heading rule uses - and the words come from the approved source definition rather than from the _LEGAL keyword set the proxy uses. For each heading the distance to the next taken block is measured.

contingency_shaped_headings.text: Risks related to Legal Proceedings and Regulations
Our pending legal proceedings could have a material adverse impact on us.
Note 17 — Commitments, Contingencies and Other Items
RISKS RELATED TO GOVERNMENT REGULATION AND LEGAL PROCEEDINGS:
Our stock price is likely to be volatile and could subject us to litigation.

result: twenty-one headings across eleven filings. Every Commitments and Contingencies note in every filing is reached, at gaps of one to fifty-seven blocks. Three headings are never reached and all three are correct: Macy's '14. Commitments' is purchase obligations for merchandise, outsourcing, software licences and energy supply; Lumen's 'Contractual Commitments' and 'Purchase Commitments' are subsections after Note 17's legal part, which is taken. The four Item 1A headings are risk-factor headings, which belong to D03's scope and not to D02's.
the_direction_nobody_had_measured: every D02 reading so far judged the excerpts that were taken. A dropped disclosure is invisible to that. Reading all of a declared range by hand is not feasible for eleven filings - Macy's alone is 1,208 blocks - so this asks a narrower question that can be answered mechanically and does not reuse the selector's own signal: does any filing carry a note heading naming contingencies, legal proceedings, litigation or commitments that the excerpt set never reaches?
what_this_does_not_establish: that nothing was dropped. This scan is itself a proxy: it finds heading-shaped blocks containing four words. A contingency disclosure under differently worded heading, or under none, would not be found. What it establishes is narrower and was previously unknown - no contingencies note in any of the eleven filings goes unreached.
